### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**27** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 30f23fef481c89e8e94beb45f6b912d56dea0ea1`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/api/v1/data (route, 50 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 30f23fef481c89e8e94beb45f6b912d56dea0ea1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b419c97045423e7af2eb6b60dc7e88f5e117bb83` — the merge of head `a0f8cfb56f18b996a72a5edb3fb396710823f849` into base `30f23fef481c89e8e94beb45f6b912d56dea0ea1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b419c97045423e7af2eb6b60dc7e88f5e117bb83 && git checkout b419c97045423e7af2eb6b60dc7e88f5e117bb83
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 30f23fef481c89e8e94beb45f6b912d56dea0ea1 a0f8cfb56f18b996a72a5edb3fb396710823f849 && git checkout -B drift-repro 30f23fef481c89e8e94beb45f6b912d56dea0ea1 && git merge --no-ff a0f8cfb56f18b996a72a5edb3fb396710823f849

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 30f23fef481c89e8e94beb45f6b912d56dea0ea1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 30f23fef481c89e8e94beb45f6b912d56dea0ea1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`

### ① Derived judgments

- Face: declared-output change on six MCP tools' error results (`Clause-②: yes` on the claim 6711692486, PR body and changeset). No path under `packages/spec/**` or `packages/types/**`, no governed path, no new error code. Diff read in full: 4 files, +318/−33.
- **One classifier, never a copy.** `dataDoorAnswerOf` reads `mapDataError` (`@objectstack/types`) — the function `/api/v1/data` answers with — for `code`, sentence and status; `rowRefusalOf` (`delete_records`) now reads the same helper. MCP and the data door cannot drift on a code-less throw.
- **Coded path first and unchanged.** `dataDoorErrorResult` asks `thrownRefusalEnvelope` before the door, so a thrown `code` renders byte for byte as before (CONTROL pinned, unique-violation spelling included); the non-record tools keep `errorResultWithCode` (CONTROL pinned).
- **No leak a REST 500 would sanitize.** A fault answers `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` / `Internal server error`, a declared 5xx's prose is withheld, and the message reaches the operator through the shared `logServerFault` line; 4xx refusals are not logged (pinned).
- **The ruled answers:** undeclared sandboxed abort → `HOOK_ABORTED` + inner sentence, hook name absent (also when the `SandboxError` instance is lost); declared 4xx kept; crash → 500; `{statusCode:503}` → 503, no invented code. Ablation on the classification: 19 red.
- **Test edits checked, not loosened:** the aggregate FLS fixture now throws coded — verified against the real throwers (`PermissionDeniedError` in plugin-security, `fieldReadDeniedError`, the plugin-audit and plugin-approvals guards all carry `PERMISSION_DENIED`/403); the `RLS: not permitted` fixture is a code-less `Error`, which the door answers as a fault, now pinned exactly.

### ② Semver level

- The accept set is unchanged; only error-result bodies move (bare text → the JSON envelope the coded path already uses; fault prose withheld). Additive-to-safer output change ⇒ patch, as the changeset declares, with the migration sentence (`error.message`, branch on `error.code`). Not a narrowing: no call that succeeded now fails.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Security: improves — internal fault text and hook names no longer reach the agent on these six tools.
- Not closed here, filed: a CODED sandboxed refusal still carries the wrapper and hook name on MCP, and the other MCP faces' divergences → #31246. `delete_records`' outer catch keeps its own sentences on purpose (they would trip `mapDataError`'s unknown-object heuristic).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-vvleyi`
Reviewed-by: `session_017ihL2dLQEXWGsE2SZ3Qn5F`

**VERDICT: PASS**
